# pinka command

`pinka` operates a provisioned lab host. Bootstrap installs it to `/usr/local/bin/pinka` and writes the lab description `/etc/pinka/lab.json` it reads (see [Doctor checks](../doctor-checks.md) and [Exit codes](../exit-codes.md)).

```text
pinka [-h] [--config FILE] [--version] COMMAND ...
```

Operate a Pokus lab host: health checks, fingerprint, start and stop, backups, golden images, researchers, inference node pairing, host updates, the documentation and uninstall.

## Global options

Every command also accepts `-h`, `--help`.

| Option | Value | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-h`, `--help` | — | — | show the help of pinka or of a command and exit |
| `--config` | `FILE` | `/etc/pinka/lab.json` | lab description written by bootstrap |
| `--version` | — | — | show program's version number and exit |

## Commands

| Command | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `pinka preflight` | run preflight read-only |
| `pinka doctor` | run the health and security checks (root) |
| `pinka status` | units, containers, Incus instances, the GPU and its arbiter, disk and last backup |
| `pinka gpu` | the GPU arbiter's requests: status, serve, train, idle (root) |
| `pinka gpu status` | the mode, the running job and the last transitions |
| `pinka gpu serve` | serve a deployment (vLLM restarts if needed) |
| `pinka gpu train` | start a training run of the active platform |
| `pinka gpu idle` | stop serving, or stop the running job (it checkpoints) |
| `pinka start` | start pinka-lab.target and wait for the platform's health hook (root) |
| `pinka stop` | drain the platform, then stop its target and pinka-lab.target (root) |
| `pinka fingerprint` | print the environment fingerprint and its hash |
| `pinka backup` | back up now or list the snapshots (root) |
| `pinka restore` | run bootstrap with --restore (root) |
| `pinka uninstall` | remove what pinka installed and keep the lab's data (root) |
| `pinka images` | golden images: list, build, export |
| `pinka images list` | aliases, fingerprints, build time and export state |
| `pinka images build` | build missing images, or one blueprint (root) |
| `pinka images export` | export images that lack an export and check every export (root) |
| `pinka user` | edit the researcher list of the configuration (never the host) |
| `pinka user add` | add a researcher |
| `pinka user remove` | lock a researcher (moved to researchers_removed) |
| `pinka user keys` | replace a researcher's public keys |
| `pinka pair` | pair a lab node with an inference node over the tailnet (root) |
| `pinka pair show` | on the inference node: show a code and wait |
| `pinka pair connect` | on the lab node: pair with the inference node |
| `pinka wsl-helpers` | where the optional Windows helpers are (wsl2 only) |
| `pinka update-host` | drain, update the OS keeping the holds, bootstrap, doctor, fingerprint diff (root) |
| `pinka platform` | the lab's platform (root) |
| `pinka platform purge` | remove a replaced platform's releases, state, restricted area and database (root) |
| `pinka docs` | the documentation of the lab |
| `pinka docs serve` | serve the built documentation read-only on 127.0.0.1 |
| `pinka docs install` | install a documentation release and make it current (root only) |
| `pinka docs rollback` | switch the documentation back to the previous release (root only) |
| `pinka window` | maintenance windows: staging on production's hardware (root only) |
| `pinka window open` | record a window (production: drain and stop first) |
| `pinka window close` | remove the record (staging: stop the lab first) |
| `pinka window expire` | stop staging on shared hardware once its window has ended (run by pinka-window-expiry.timer) |


### pinka restore

Run bootstrap.sh with --restore. Bootstrap options follow `--`, as in `pinka restore -- --non-interactive`.

```text
pinka restore [-h] [BOOTSTRAP_OPTION ...]
```

| Argument | Value | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `BOOTSTRAP_OPTION` (optional) | — | — | passed to bootstrap.sh (after --) |

### pinka uninstall

Run bootstrap.sh --uninstall from the checkout recorded in /etc/pinka/bootstrap-state.json: the removal plan first, then a backup offer and the typed machine name. Further bootstrap options follow `--`, as in `pinka uninstall -- --non-interactive --confirm-machine lab1`.

```text
pinka uninstall [-h] [--dry-run] [--purge-data] [--skip-backup]
                       [--json]
                       [BOOTSTRAP_OPTION ...]
```

| Argument | Value | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--dry-run` | — | — | print the plan and change nothing |
| `--purge-data` | — | — | also remove the lab's data (the machine name is typed a second time) |
| `--skip-backup` | — | — | do not offer a backup first |
| `--json` | — | — | print the plan or the report as JSON |
| `BOOTSTRAP_OPTION` (optional) | — | — | passed to bootstrap.sh (after --) |

### pinka docs serve

Serve the built documentation read-only on 127.0.0.1.

```text
pinka docs serve [-h] [--dir DIR] [--port PORT]
```

| Argument | Value | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--dir` | `DIR` | — | built documentation site (default: docs.dir of the lab description, /usr/local/share/pinka/docs) |
| `--port` | `PORT` | — | port (default: docs.port of the lab description, 18706) |

### pinka docs install

Verify a docs release tarball against its SHA-256, unpack it into a new version directory (refusing absolute paths, .. and links that leave it), switch current to it in one step and keep the three most recent versions.

```text
pinka docs install [-h] --sha256 SUM [--version NAME] tarball
```

| Argument | Value | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tarball` | — | — | the release's documentation tarball |
| `--sha256` | `SUM` | — | the tarball's SHA-256 (published with it) |
| `--version` | `NAME` | — | version directory name (default: the tarball's file name without its suffix) |

### pinka docs rollback

Switch current back to the version installed before it.

```text
pinka docs rollback [-h]
```

### pinka window

Open or close a maintenance window, recorded in /etc/pinka/maintenance-window.json on each side. On production, open drains and stops the lab first and it stays stopped until close; staging on shared hardware starts only inside its window.

```text
pinka window [-h] ACTION ...
```

### pinka window open

Record a window (production: drain and stop first).

```text
pinka window open [-h] --start TIME --end TIME
```

| Argument | Value | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--start` | `TIME` | — | UTC start, such as 2026-10-12T18:00Z |
| `--end` | `TIME` | — | UTC end, such as 2026-10-12T22:00Z |

### pinka window close

Remove the record (staging: stop the lab first).

```text
pinka window close [-h]
```

### pinka window expire

Stop staging on shared hardware once its window has ended (run by pinka-window-expiry.timer).

```text
pinka window expire [-h]
```

Exit codes: 0 success; 1 failure (doctor: warnings only); 2 usage error (doctor: a check of severity error failed). See [Exit codes](../exit-codes.md).
